subject: Game Theory
title: Adverse Selection
description: A short lesson to help you apply Adverse Selection.

hook.text: Health insurance attracts sick people more than healthy ones. The sickest customers buy the most coverage.

buildup.text: Adverse selection occurs when the informed side self-selects in ways that hurt the uninformed side.

discovery.text: Insurers respond by raising premiums, which drives healthy people away—making the pool sicker and costlier.

twist.text: This death spiral can collapse entire markets. Without intervention, some risks become uninsurable.

climax.text: The Affordable Care Act's individual mandate forced healthy people to buy insurance to prevent collapse.

punchline.text: The wrong customers show up first.

quiz.question: What causes adverse selection in insurance?
options: High-risk individuals are more likely to buy coverage
